title: Adaptive KV-spill preemption and batch-shape profiles for long-context model variants
creator: Ava Park
description: Goal: reduce p99 tail-latency and OOMs for long-context variants (Llama-extended, Mistral-long, Qwen-32k) by combining adaptive KV-spill preemption with batch-shape profiles tuned per model variant. Motivation: current static spill thresholds and fixed max_batch settings lead to either excessive KV churn (high eviction rate, fragmentation) or conservative batching (lower throughput). This ticket implements a) predictive spill-preemption heuristic that triggers early lightweight eviction of low-priority KV slices during microbursts, b) per-variant batch-shape profiles that adapt target batch sizes based on recent sequence length distribution and observed KV residency, and c) an allocator tuning pass to reduce fragmentation during repeated spills.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency unchanged and p99 latency reduced by >= 12% on long-context workloads compared to baseline
KV eviction rate reduced by >= 20% under synthetic microburst traces while maintaining cache hit-rate >= 92%
Zero customer-facing OOM incidents in 48h soak on dedicated test pools running 32k-config variants
Telemetry surfaced in console: kv_evictions/sec, spill_preempt_count, batch_shape_mode, fragmentation_index
design_summary: 1) Spill preemption: compute per-request spill_score = residency_pressure * layer_priority_weight - kv_age_factor. When spill_score > adaptive_threshold, prefer evicting low-priority slices (token embeddings and attention caches for bottom layers) instead of large contiguous slabs to minimize compaction cost. Threshold is model-variant specific and learned from short-run traces. 2) Batch-shape profiles: maintain sliding distribution of sequence_length percentiles and set target_batch_size = max_batch * shape_factor(seq_percentiles, kv_hit_rate). This reduces large-batch assembly when many requests carry long prefixes (avoid KV thrash). 3) Allocator tuning: introduce epochal compaction windows during low-load tail (configurable per-pool) and tune cudaMallocAsync pool high-water marks to keep fragmentation_index decreasing over time. 4) Fallback: if preemption increases p50 latency for a customer above their SLO, revert to conservative profile per-customer using routing policy.
implementation_plan: - Spike (3 days): collect traces for Llama-Long, Mistral-XL-long, Qwen-32k across typical traffic mixes. Instrument candidate signals (residency_pressure, kv_age, per-layer footprint). - Prototype (5 days): implement spill_score calculation, eviction candidate selector, and minimal batch-shape controller. Add feature flags. - Benchmarks (4 days): run A/B on dedicated 4x A100(80GB) pools with synthetic microburst and replayed production traces. Measure p95/p99, eviction/sec, fragmentation_index. - Iterate (3 days): tune thresholds, add per-variant defaults, and safety limits. - Rollout (canary 2 weeks): route 5% traffic for each long-context model on dedicated tenants, monitor telemetry, and expand to 25/50/100% on success.
benchmarks_summary: Local A/B (replay) initial run: - Baseline p99 = 420ms, Experimental p99 = 362ms (14% reduction) - KV evictions/sec baseline = 18.2, experimental = 13.9 (23.6% reduction) - Fragmentation index improved from 0.28 -> 0.21. Observed small p50 increase (~3%) on extreme short-request mixes. Next step: validate across dedicated pools and quantized model variants.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Preemptive eviction could cause cache-miss storms for some prompt patterns. Mitigation: conservative per-customer override and short-term rollback via routing policy.
Risk: Allocator compaction can be expensive and increase latency during windows. Mitigation: only run compaction during observed low-latency buckets and throttle compaction step size.
Risk: Model-variant defaults might not generalize. Mitigation: collect per-variant telemetry and expose tuning knobs in console for on-demand adjustments.
